briefing.headline: Two Boston-based B2B marketing reqs are live at CarGurus — and the enterprise sponsors (Adobe, Workday, Nvidia) are hiding under low keyword scores.
briefing.focus: Spend the first 10 minutes on the two Boston roles (CarGurus B2B + Brand Marketing Specialist) — local, public company, specialist-level, no relocation story to explain. Spend the next 10 on the keyword-scorer's blind spot: Adobe's B2B Performance Marketing Specialist and Workday's Paid Media & ABX Campaign Manager both scored 60 because their JDs never loaded, but 'ABX' is literally ABM and both are top-20 H-1B sponsors. Skip the Amazon 'AMZ#####' analyst postings entirely — those are PERM immigration-compliance notices, not open reqs.

ranked.why: Boston HQ, B2B, 'Specialist' level — the single cleanest lane+level+location match on the board; public company with a real sponsorship track record.
PMM in Boston at the #1 H-1B sponsor in tech — rare combination; req is aging (posted 6/29) so apply now or drop it.
Adobe scored 60 only because the JD never loaded — B2B performance marketing at Specialist level, top-tier sponsor, is a near-perfect profile match.
'ABX' is ABM under a different brand name — this is the candidate's headline skill at a company that sponsors hundreds of visas a year, and the scorer missed it completely.
6sense IS the ABM platform — selling it means the resume's top skill is the product; remote-US and never surfaced before.
Remote-USA performance marketing at a public fintech — the banking/fintech background is a differentiator here, not just background noise.
Second Boston CarGurus req at the same level — apply to both; brand is a slight lane stretch but proximity outweighs it.
Marketing analytics inside AWS demand gen — the exact intersection of both target lanes at the strongest sponsor; only demoted because it's been recommended three times.
Remote-US marketing analyst on funnel/PLG metrics — MQL-to-pipeline work the resume already owns; four runs in, so decide yes or no today.
Remote-US GTM analytics with SQL + funnel ownership; 'Manager' here is an IC title, not a people-leader step up.
The title is literally 'Audience and Messaging' — positioning and segmentation are the two strongest lines on the resume.
Remote-US lifecycle marketing on a lending product — six years of banking domain knowledge is a real edge over generic SaaS applicants.
Boston, strong sponsor, Salesforce-centric GTM systems — leans ops rather than marketing, but local roles are scarce enough to justify it.
Scored 60 on a truncated HTML blob — a payments/stablecoin PMM role is one of the best fintech-background plays on this list.
Prospecting campaigns and pipeline measurement at AWS, badly under-scored at 61; demand gen is core resume territory.
B2B SaaS product marketing for a full product line at Amazon — the 64 score reflects vocabulary, not fit.
Remote-US regional/field marketing scored 61 for no good reason; remote US is worth a lot given the Boston base.
Remote-US demand gen program ownership — clean lane match; Grafana is mid-size, so confirm sponsorship early.
Remote-US and 'Specialist' level at a public company — one of the few roles here that is unambiguously not too senior.
Email architecture and audience segmentation at AWS maps directly to the Eloqua/HubSpot lifecycle experience.
Promotions analytics is marketing analytics with a different label — closest thing to a marketing analyst req in Amazon's BA family.
'Associate' marketing automation manager is exactly the right level and the Eloqua skill transfers; demoted only for being pushed three runs running.
Waltham MA is commutable and the 61 score undersells it — but verify this is GTM strategy, not customer-facing professional services.
Associate-level paid social with A/B testing and attribution ownership — right level, strong sponsor, real growth-marketing reps.
Associate field marketing for the East region at Datadog — level-appropriate and the closest Datadog gets to a Boston orbit.
US-Remote GTM planning at a company where the fintech background reads as domain expertise rather than a pivot.
Straight PMM ownership of a product launch at a strong sponsor; NYC-only and technical depth is the hurdle, not the marketing craft.
Fully remote GTM business ops with funnel and pipeline analytics — public company, and the 90 ATS score means the resume parses cleanly.
Boston analyst role, but four runs of no action suggests it's already been passed on; mid-size hardware company, sponsorship unproven.
Nvidia sponsors heavily and enterprise AI PMM is on-lane, but the technical bar and Santa Clara location both cut against it.
Campaign management is the least technical Nvidia marketing req on the board — the best entry point into a major sponsor.
Demand gen at a fintech-adjacent company is a genuine fit, but four runs without action says this one isn't landing.
Large established sponsor, campaign marketing on-lane, six locations — worth a low-effort application.
One of the few Amazon BA II reqs that is an actual open role rather than a PERM notice; domain is infrastructure, not marketing.
Growth marketing for SMB advertisers is on-lane, but OpenAI's hiring bar and SF-only make this a long shot.
Field marketing is a clean lane fit; extremely competitive and SF/NYC-only.
ABM and partner marketing at AWS — direct skill match, but Seattle-based and one of many near-identical Amazon partner reqs.
Scored 100 but it's insurance operations wearing an analyst title — four runs deep with no bite; treat the 100 as noise.
Legitimate sales ops analytics, but no Boston or remote option and the keyword score badly overstates the marketing overlap.
